articles.title: SJAA Annual Membership Meeting Report
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) held its annual Membership Meeting on February 3, 2018, which included board elections where four incumbents were re-elected. The event celebrated four members—David Grover, Glenn Newell, Sukhada Palav, and Teruo Utsumi—for their significant contributions to outreach, astrophotography, and club programs. The meeting also announced the resignation of President Teruo Utsumi due to health issues, concluding with a potluck and welcoming new members.

articles.title: Lunar Eclipse from the USS Hornet - Alameda, CA
articles.summary: This article reports on a lunar eclipse viewing event held aboard the USS Hornet in Alameda, CA. Attendees, including members of the Eastbay Astronomy Society and SJAA, enjoyed a unique vantage point to observe and photograph the eclipsed moon as it set spectacularly over the San Francisco skyline. The event also offered the opportunity to explore the historic aircraft carrier, known for its role in the Apollo space program.

articles.title: Falcon Heavy: A Multi-User Spaceport Success
articles.summary: The article highlights the successful demonstration flight of the SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from Launch Complex 39A, marking a significant milestone for NASA's Kennedy Space Center (KSC) as a premier multi-user spaceport. Through property and Space Act Agreements, NASA supports commercial partners like SpaceX, providing essential services and infrastructure, which is crucial for the expansion of commercial spaceflight alongside NASA's own deep-space exploration programs like SLS and Orion. This transformation allows KSC to host diverse launch capabilities for both commercial and future crewed missions.

articles.title: Rocket Girls and the Advent of the Space Age
articles.summary: The article highlights the crucial role of "human computers," predominantly women, at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in the early days of space exploration. Their manual calculations were instrumental in the successful launch of Explorer 1, America's first satellite. These women, including Janez Lawson, the first African American hired in a technical role at JPL, also represented a significant step forward for women and underrepresented groups in technical fields traditionally dominated by men.

articles.title: SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery
articles.summary: The article showcases a gallery of astrophotography contributed by members of the SJAA (San Jose Astronomical Association) in March 2018. It features images of celestial objects like the Rosette Nebula, Pencil Nebula, and Melotte 15, along with a star trails photograph from Arches National Park. Each entry details the equipment, imaging parameters, location, and processing software used by the photographers.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: This article, titled "Kid Spot," offers an engaging and educational segment for children, featuring moon-related jokes and a quiz on lunar facts. It also provides a detailed explanation of a "super blue blood Moon" eclipse that occurred on January 31, clarifying what constitutes a supermoon, blue moon, and blood moon. The content blends lighthearted entertainment with scientific information about lunar phenomena.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: This article from the Board of Directors announces a Spring Swap Meet scheduled for March 11th. It details excerpts from recent board meetings where topics such as star party policy, the search for an audit firm, and complimentary memberships were discussed. Key organizational changes include the resignation of Teruo Utsumi as President and board member, with Vice-President Bill O'Neill temporarily taking over, and the introduction of Emi Nikolov as the new Production Editor, replacing Tom Piller.

articles.title: SJAA Programs and Resources
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a wide array of programs and resources for its members and the community, including a library, free telescope fix-it sessions, and solar observing events. They also provide comprehensive educational programs like Quick STARt and Intro to the Night Sky, an equipment loaner program, and specialized groups for astro-imaging. SJAA actively engages in community outreach by hosting school star parties and regularly publishes a newsletter.
